title: Residue-field finite-model criterion for J-2
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ and every finite purely inseparable field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], with $R\to L$ the residue-field map followed by the given extension, there is an $R$-subalgebra $B\subseteq L$ which is finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], whose fractions $b/c$ ($b,c\in B$, $c\ne0$) exhaust $L$, and for which $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $U$ such that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak q\in U$. Then for every finite type $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] the subset $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:A_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open. Equivalently, $R$ satisfies the J-2 condition of [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (4) implies (1), with J-0 and J-2 expanded using definition-J (Tag 07P7). The domain model is embedded in its specified fraction field L.

proof.text: First prove that every finite type $R$-algebra $S$ which is a domain has a nonempty regular open. Fix such an $S$, generated by $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ over $R$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $\mathfrak p=\ker(R\to S)$, a prime because $S$ is a domain, and let $K$ be the field of fractions of $S$. The residue field $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ embeds into $K$: its element $(r+\mathfrak p)/(u+\mathfrak p)$, $u\notin\mathfrak p$, maps to the fraction of the images of $r,u$ in $S$. In $R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, two such fractions $r/u$ and $r'/u'$ are equal exactly when $ru'-r'u\in\mathfrak p$: multiplying by the unit denominators reduces this to $(ru'-r'u)/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, and the localization equivalence and primality give that condition exactly. Their images in $K$ are equal exactly when $ru'-r'u$ maps to zero in $S$, which is the same condition since $\ker(R\to S)=\mathfrak p$. Thus the formula is well-defined and injective; the fraction formulas for addition and multiplication show it is a field homomorphism. Every element of $K$ is a quotient of polynomials in the $s_i$ over the image of $R$, so $K=k(s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ is finitely generated as a field over $k$.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, proof of (4) implies (2): choice of S, p, K.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] to the finitely generated field extension $K/k$. Obtain a commutative square $k\to L\to K'$, $k\to K\to K'$ in which $L/k$ and $K'/K$ are finite purely inseparable and $K'/L$ is separable. Identify the fields with their images in $K'$; field homomorphisms are injective because their kernels are proper ideals in fields. This gives exactly a finite purely inseparable extension of the specified residue field to which the hypothesis on $R$ applies.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, field diagram; algebra.tex Tag 030R, lemma-make-separable, first assertion (already provided by the existing node).

proof.text: Choose the finite $R$-subalgebra $B\subseteq L$ from the hypothesis, with fraction field $L$ and a nonempty regular open. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. Choose $R$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $B$. Inside $K'$ define $S'$ to be the subring consisting of finite sums $\sum_i u_i v_i$ with $u_i\in S$, $v_i\in B$. The empty sum is $0$, and $1=1\cdot1$ belongs to this set. Concatenating sums and replacing each $u_i$ by $-u_i$ prove closure under addition and negatives; distributing products and using $(uv)(u^\prime v^\prime)=(uu^\prime)(vv^\prime)$ proves closure under multiplication. Hence it is a subring. The expressions $s=s\cdot1$ and $b=1\cdot b$ show that it contains $S$ and $B$. Since $S=R[s_1,\ldots,s_n]$ and $B$ contains the image of $R$, one has $S'=B[s_1,\ldots,s_n]$. Also every sum $\sum_i u_i v_i$ becomes an $S$-linear combination of the $b_j$ by expanding each $v_i$ as an $R$-linear combination. Thus $S'$ is finite as an $S$-module, and in particular is generated as an $S$-algebra by the $b_j$. Both $B\to S'$ and $S\to S'$ are injective finite type maps of domains.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2: the image of S tensor_R B in K prime, with its two finite type structures written out.

proof.text: Let $M\subseteq K'$ be the field of fractions of $S'$. It contains $K$ and $L$, since $S\subseteq S'$ and $B\subseteq S'$ and these fields consist of fractions of elements of $S$ and $B$. Conversely $S'\subseteq KL$, the smallest subfield of $K'$ containing $K$ and $L$, so $M=KL=L(s_1,\ldots,s_n)$. In particular $M$ need not equal $K'$. The extension $M/L$ is separable by [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every finitely generated intermediate field between $L$ and $M$ is also one between $L$ and $K'$, and is therefore separably generated because $K'/L$ is separable. This proves all quantifiers in that definition for $M/L$.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, fraction field assertion corrected from K prime to the compositum KL; algebra.tex Tag 030O, definition-separable-field-extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-j0-separable-finite-type-ascent] to $B\to S'$. The base $B$ is Noetherian, both rings are domains, the map is injective and finite type by step 3, the induced fraction field extension is $M/L$ and is separable by step 4, and the required nonempty regular open of $B$ was chosen from the hypothesis. Therefore $S'$ has a nonempty regular open. Apply [lem-exc-j0-finite-type-domain-descent] to $S\to S'$: its base $S$ is Noetherian by step 1, its map is injective finite type by step 3, and its target is a domain with a nonempty regular open. Conclude that $S$ has a nonempty regular open. Since the finite type domain $S$ was arbitrary, this conclusion holds for every such $R$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, last two sentences of (4) implies (2), citing Tags 07PB and 07PA.

proof.text: Now fix any finite type $R$-algebra $A$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, the quotient $S=A/\mathfrak q$ is a domain and is finite type over $R$: the images of any finite set of algebra generators of $A$ generate the quotient. Hence step 5 gives a nonempty regular open of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak q)$. Apply [lem-exc-regular-locus-open-from-prime-quotients] with this $A$ and these opens for all primes to conclude that the regular locus of $A$ is open. If $A$ is the zero ring there are no primes and the same criterion gives the empty open regular locus.

proof.text: The preceding openness assertion for every finite type $R$-algebra is exactly the J-2 condition expanded in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. This proves both formulations of the conclusion.
